title: Boundary point classes commute with field extension
statement: Let k and k' be algebraically closed fields with a k-algebra structure on k' [def-sc-field-extension], let f:C to Spec k be a smooth affine connected curve [def-sc-curves], and let c be a smooth connected compactification [lem-sc-compactification] of relative dimension one before and after base change [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. There is a bijection between the boundary closed points of c.Z and those of its base change, such that Picard pullback [def-sc-picard-group] sends the class O(P) [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] to the class O(e(P)). No boundary base point or boundary subgroup is chosen.

source.place: Affine case, compactification/boundary and final compatibility paragraphs; expanded from the proof recorded in lem-sc-pic-affine-base-change-compatibility

proof.text: Install regularity and irreducibility of the smooth connected ambient curve. The range of the open immersion is nonempty. IsOpen.isClosed_singleton_of_mem_compl in dimension one shows that every point outside it is closed. The cartesian open-immersion square (Compactification.isPullback_i_ofIsPullback and Scheme.range_snd_of_isPullback) identifies the new open range with the inverse image of the old one. Thus projection sends every new boundary point to an old closed boundary point. Finiteness of the complement is not needed.

For every old closed point P, pointOfClosedPoint constructs its rational section using algebraic closedness and finite type. Apply Scheme.Hom.baseChangeFieldPoint to get a rational section over k prime; it is a closed immersion, hence gives a closed point upstairs. The projection returns P. Scheme.Hom.baseChangeFieldPoint_eq_of_fst_eq proves that this is the unique point over P. Restrict the projection to the boundary subtypes, prove injectivity by this uniqueness and surjectivity by the lifted sections, and take the inverse of Equiv.ofBijective. Its inverse law gives the pointwise projection identity he.

For a boundary point P construct its rational section p and base-changed section q. Uniqueness of the fibre identifies the point of q with e(P). Cancel the ambient base-change square from the outer identity square using IsPullback.of_bot to obtain IsPullback b q p projection. Scheme.ker_pointOfClosedPoint identifies ker(p) with the reduced point ideal I; map_vanishingIdeal applied to the reduced one-point source identifies ker(q) with the new point ideal J. The proved source theorem Scheme.Hom.ker_of_isPullback (flat base change of kernel ideals, with p a quasi-compact closed immersion and the projection flat) gives I.comap projection = J.

Smoothness of relative dimension one makes I and J invertible. Apply IdealSheafData.IsInvertible.nonempty_pullback_dual_toModules_iso to I and its identified invertible pullback J. Compose this isomorphism with the Picard skeleton representative isomorphisms and use Pic.eq_iff_nonempty_iso. This gives exactly the displayed equality for each P, completing the unchanged existential statement.

proof_origin.place: Affine boundary paragraph; second reading replaces the false arbitrary-bijection lemma by a direct proof using proved source rational-point fibre, kernel-pullback and invertible-ideal pullback declarations

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_point_class_base_change
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k']
    {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [Smooth c.g]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g]
    [hsm' : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (c.baseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).g]
    : let b := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
      let c' := c.baseChange b
      ∃ e : {P : closedPoints c.Z // P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base} ≃
          {Q : closedPoints c'.Z // Q.val ∉ Set.range c'.i.base},
        ∀ P, Scheme.Pic.mapHom (pullback.fst c.g b)
          (@Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P.val) =
          @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k' _ c'.Z ⟨c'.g⟩ hsm' (e P).val
